Q: Not able to access local server running after VPN connection A:

If you are using Gradio, Flask, FastAPI, etc., you can simply add this line to your code, and everything will work correctly. This line implies that localhost and other forms of localhost don't use a proxy

import os

os.environ["NO_PROXY"] = "localhost,127.0.0.1,::1,.local"

Q: Lambda in max returns weird value A:

Your key function is used for the comparison (not filtering). In your case, it returns True for even numbers and False for odd numbers. True is treated as 1 in numerical contexts, and False is 0.

print([x % 2 == 0 for x in L])
# [False, True, True, True, False, False, True, False]

print([int(x % 2 == 0) for x in L])
# [0, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0, 1, 0]

So it's actually just comparing 0's and 1's to see which is highest/max, which is 1 in this case.

And what happens when there are many max's or many 1's? From the docs for max:

If multiple items are maximal, the function returns the first one encountered.

2 is the first item which had the max-key of 1, so it returns 2.

If you want the maximum even number, then filter for it first, with a list comprehension or generator expression and then find max.

even_nums = [x for x in L if x % 2 == 0]
# even_nums is [2, 10, 4, 14]

print(max(even_nums))
# 14

Or as a one liner with a generator-expression:

print(max(x for x in L if x % 2 == 0))

Q: Slow HikariDataSource.getConnection() on slow on low traffic, fast on big traffic A:

You can set idleTimeout when minimumIdle is defined as less than maximumPoolSize

⌚idleTimeout This property controls the maximum amount of time that a connection is allowed to sit idle in the pool. This setting only applies when minimumIdle is defined to be less than maximumPoolSize. Idle connections will not be retired once the pool reaches minimumIdle connections.

Q: Spark - UbuntuVM - insufficient memory for the Java Runtime Environment A:

We need to set spark.executor.memory in conf/spark-defaults.conf file to a value specific to your machine. For example,

usr1@host:~/spark-1.6.1$ cp conf/spark-defaults.conf.template conf/spark-defaults.conf
nano conf/spark-defaults.conf
spark.driver.memory              512m

For more information, refer to the official documentation: http://spark.apache.org/docs/latest/configuration.html

Q: Resizing Image and fit it to the Canvas size A:

All you need to do is figure out the size you should resize to while

  • Making it all fit inside the window, and
  • Preserving the original aspect ratio.

Thankfully that's not hard to do.

 def best_fit(oldsize, picsize):
    new_width, new_height = picsize
    old_width, old_height = oldsize
    # if new_width/old_width < new_height/old_height is mathematically the same as
    if new_width * old_height < new_height * old_width:
        # reduce height to keep original aspect ratio
        new_height = max(1, old_height * new_width // old_width)
    else:
        # reduce width to keep original aspect ratio
        new_width = max(1, old_width * new_height // old_height)
    return (new_width, new_height)

siz = self.image.size
self.image = self.image.resize(best_fit(siz, picsize), Image.ANTIALIAS)

The max calls keep the width and height from going to zero.

Q: Customized org-capture-template for Org Capture Extension A:

Still using the %(sexp) syntax, you could use this function in the template org-insert-last-stored-link.

This is the native function for inserting links so Org ought to take care of escaping characters that need to be escaped.

Your Org template would become:

     ("L" "Protocol Link" entry (file+headline "~/web.org" "Links")
      "* (with-temp-buffer (org-insert-last-stored-link 1) (buffer-string))\n")

You'll see that in this answer I combine this with With-temp-buffer, which makes it slightly less simple, but when the answer was originally written it was simple.

Though on Org-mode version 9.7 (latest in May 2025) square brackets don't seem to be a problem anymore. The following looks just fine on an org document:

** [[https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.04838][[1606.04838] Optimization Methods for Large-Scale Machine Learning]]
